_why: Committed byte-identical to BOTH repos, and pinned by SHA-256 in BOTH test suites — the cross-repo comparison resolves the sibling repo as a directory and SKIPS in CI, so a content digest on each side is what makes a one-sided edit fail in that repo's own workflow. Changing anything here is a four-file edit: both copies and both digests. v2 (2026-08-24) adds the `selected` action: the ACTION NAME is the entire version-skew mechanism, because a build that predates a control deletes the command it does not recognise and matches no dispatch branch — so the failure is 'nothing left the machine' rather than 'thirty runs left against a request for two'. Over-collection is the harm here, so the failure has to point that way. Reusing `send-logs-limited` with a new field would have failed the OTHER way: the older handler reads only `runs` and would ignore an unknown selection, collecting the newest N. `maxRuns` is also the maximum slider position the app can send, so if the two repos disagree about it a control states one thing and the machine does another with nothing failing anywhere.
